tool.name: Collection from table
tool.description: one element per value of column 1, empty elements kept
tool.command: mkdir out && awk -F'\t' '!seen[\$1]++ { print \$1 }' '$table' > table_ids.txt && #if $identifiers tr -d '\r' < '$identifiers' | grep -v '^\$' > ids.txt && #else cp table_ids.txt ids.txt && #end if awk -v FS='\t' -v ext='$ext' -f '$split_script' '$table' ids.txt

configfiles.configfile: # first file: the table, rows collected per value of column 1 (column 1 removed) NR == FNR { id = $1 sub(/^[^\t]*\t?/, "") rows[id] = rows[id] $0 "\n" next } # second file: one element per identifier, in this order; no rows gives an empty element { i++ name = $0 gsub(/\//, "_", name) f = sprintf("out/%06d_%s.%s", i, name, ext) printf "%s", rows[$0] > f close(f) }

param.name: table
param.label: Table
param.help: Column 1 is the element identifier, the other columns are written to that element (one line per row).

param.name: identifiers
param.label: Element identifiers
param.help: One identifier per line: the elements of the collection, in this order. An identifier without rows in the table gets an empty element. Without this file the elements follow the first appearance in column 1.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Turns a table into a list collection: every row goes to the element named in column 1, without that column. With a file of identifiers, the collection has exactly those elements in that order, and an identifier that has no row gets an **empty** element, the same as a per-element step that produced nothing. Without it, the elements follow the first appearance of each identifier.
Typical use: compute a per-sample result for all samples in one job (one table), then turn it back into the per-sample collection that following per-sample tools expect.
**Example**
Table::
s1 chr19 33792951 33792951 s2 chr13 28592642 28592642
Identifiers ``s2``, ``s6``, ``s1`` give the elements s2 (``chr13 28592642 28592642``), s6 (empty) and s1 (``chr19 33792951 33792951``).
